summary: Python cannot find a module called '<name>'.
causes: The package '<name>' is not installed in the environment running your script.
The module name is misspelled.
It is installed in a different environment (check the interpreter selected in VS Code and your venv).
It is your own file, but it is in another folder or named differently.
fix: Install it in the same environment with pip, then run again. Some packages install under a different name (cv2 = opencv-python, PIL = pillow, sklearn = scikit-learn, yaml = pyyaml).

summary: '<name>' does not exist inside '<module>'.
causes: A typo in the name '<name>'.
Your installed version of '<module>' is older or newer and does not have it.
A circular import (two of your files import each other).
Your own file is named the same as a library (for example random.py), so it shadows the real one.
fix: Check the spelling, upgrade the package, rename any file that shares a name with a library, and avoid circular imports.

summary: The name '<name>' is used before it exists.
causes: A typo in the variable or function name (Python is case sensitive).
The variable is used before it is assigned.
A missing import for '<name>'.
The variable was defined inside a function and is used outside it.
fix: Check the spelling, define '<name>' before using it, or import it at the top of the file.
example:
import <name>   # if it is a module
<name> = 0      # if it is a variable

summary: The local variable '<name>' is used before it gets a value.
causes: You assign to '<name>' somewhere inside the function, which makes Python treat it as local everywhere in that function.
The assignment happens only inside an if/loop that did not run.
fix: Give '<name>' a starting value at the top of the function, or declare it with 'global <name>' if you really mean the outer variable.

summary: You tried to join text with a non-text value using +.
causes: Adding a number (or other type) to a string, such as 'Age: ' + 25.
fix: Convert the value to text with str(), or use an f-string.

summary: The operator '<op>' cannot be used between a '<a>' and a '<b>'.
causes: Mixing incompatible types, for example a number and a string.
A variable is None because a function did not return a value.
Input from input() is text and needs converting to a number.
fix: Convert both values to the same type (int(), float(), str()) and check that neither one is None.
example:
a = int(input('First: '))
b = int(input('Second: '))
print(a + b)

summary: You used [ ] on a '<t>' value, which does not support it.
causes: The value is None (a function returned nothing, or a method like list.sort() returns None).
The value is a number or another type that cannot be indexed.
A variable was overwritten with a different type.
fix: Print the variable and its type() before the failing line to see what it really holds, and make sure the function returns the value you expect.

summary: You used () on a '<t>' value, but it is not a function.
causes: A variable has the same name as a function and replaced it (for example naming a variable 'list' or 'str').
A missing operator, such as writing 5(x) instead of 5 * x.
Calling an attribute that is a value, not a method.
fix: Rename the variable that shadows the function, or add the missing operator.

summary: You tried to loop over or unpack a '<t>' value.
causes: Looping over a single number or None.
A function returned None instead of a list.
fix: Make sure the value is a list, tuple, string, etc. For a number, use range().

summary: A function was called with too few arguments (missing <n>).
causes: You left out one or more arguments in the call.
A method was called on the class instead of an object, so 'self' is missing.
fix: Pass all required arguments, or give the parameters default values. For methods, create an object first.

summary: A function expects <exp> argument(s) but received <got>.
causes: Too many arguments in the call.
A method in a class is missing 'self' as its first parameter.
fix: Match the number of arguments to the function definition, and add 'self' as the first parameter of class methods.

summary: The dictionary has no key <key>.
causes: A typo or different capitalization in the key.
The key was never added to the dictionary.
Data from a file or API is missing that field.
fix: Check the key exists first, or use .get() with a default value.

summary: You asked for a list position that does not exist.
causes: The index is bigger than the last position (lists start at 0, so a list of 3 items ends at index 2).
The list is empty.
An off-by-one mistake in a loop, such as range(len(x) + 1).
fix: Check the length before indexing, and loop with range(len(my_list)) or directly over the items.

summary: You used '.<attr>' on None, meaning a variable holds no value.
causes: A function did not return anything (it returned None).
A method that changes the object in place (like list.sort() or list.append()) was assigned to a variable.
A search such as re.match() or a lookup found nothing.
fix: Check the value is not None before using it, and make sure your function has a return statement.

summary: The module '<module>' has no '<attr>'.
causes: A typo in '<attr>'.
Your own file is named '<module>.py' and is hiding the real library.
An older version of the library does not include it.
fix: Rename any of your files that share a name with a library, delete its __pycache__ folder, check the spelling, and update the library.

summary: A '<obj>' has no attribute or method named '<attr>'.
causes: A typo or wrong capitalization in '<attr>'.
The variable is a different type than you expect.
Using a method from another type (for example a list method on a string).
fix: Print type() of the variable and use dir() to see what it supports.

summary: The file or folder '<path>' was not found.
causes: A typo in the file name or extension.
The script is running from a different folder than you expect.
The file has not been created or moved yet.
fix: Check the exact path, or build it from the script location so it works from anywhere.
example:
from pathlib import Path
path = Path(__file__).parent / 'data.txt'
print(path.exists())

summary: Python cannot find the file or path you gave it.
causes: Wrong file name, extension or folder.
The program runs from a different working directory.
fix: Print os.getcwd() to see where Python is looking, and use a full path or a path relative to your script.

summary: Python is not allowed to access this file or folder.
causes: The file is open in another program (common with Excel files).
You are opening a folder as if it were a file.
The file or folder needs admin rights.
fix: Close other programs using the file, check you are pointing at a file and not a folder, and check file permissions.

summary: You divided a number by zero.
causes: A variable that should not be zero is zero (empty list length, missing data).
A calculation produced 0 earlier in the program.
fix: Check the divisor before dividing.

pattern: invalid literal for int\(\) with base (?P<base>\d+): (?P<value>.+)
summary: The text <value> cannot be turned into a whole number.
causes: The text contains letters, spaces, symbols or a decimal point.
The input is empty.
A float written as text, such as '3.5', passed to int().
fix: Validate or clean the text before converting, and catch the error.

pattern: could not convert string to float: (?P<value>.+)
summary: The text <value> cannot be turned into a decimal number.
causes: The text has letters, commas or currency symbols.
The text is empty.
fix: Remove unwanted characters and wrap the conversion in try/except.

summary: The number of variables does not match the number of values.
causes: Unpacking a list or tuple into the wrong number of variables.
A split() produced more or fewer parts than expected.
fix: Print the value to check its length and match the variable count, or use a starred variable for the rest.

summary:
A '
' was opened but never closed.
causes: A missing closing bracket, parenthesis or brace, often on this line or just above it.
fix: Count your opening and closing brackets in the reported line and the lines above it.

summary: A colon is missing.
causes: Statements like if, for, while, def, class, else and try must end with a colon.
fix: Add ':' at the end of the line.

summary: A text string was opened but not closed.
causes: A missing closing quote.
Mixing single and double quotes, or an apostrophe inside a single-quoted string.
fix: Close the string with the same quote you opened it with, or wrap the text in the other kind of quote.

summary: print needs parentheses in Python 3.
causes: The code was written in Python 2 style.
fix: Put the text inside parentheses.

summary: Python cannot understand the code on the reported line.
causes: A missing or extra bracket, quote, comma or colon on this line or the line above.
Using = (assign) where == (compare) is needed.
A misspelled keyword.
Code copied with special characters, like curly quotes.
fix: Look at the reported line and the one before it, and check for unmatched brackets or quotes, missing colons and typos.

summary: A line is indented when it should not be.
causes: Extra spaces or an extra tab at the start of the line.
fix: Line the code up with the surrounding lines, and use 4 spaces consistently.

summary: A block needs at least one indented line under it.
causes: The body after if, for, def, class and similar statements is empty or not indented.
fix: Indent the next line by 4 spaces, or use 'pass' as a placeholder.

summary: The indentation is inconsistent.
causes: Mixing tabs and spaces.
A line is indented to a level that does not match any block above it.
fix: Use 4 spaces everywhere. In VS Code, use 'Convert Indentation to Spaces' from the Command Palette.

summary: A function kept calling itself until Python stopped it.
causes: A recursive function has no stopping condition (base case), or it never reaches it.
Two functions call each other forever.
fix: Add a base case that returns without calling the function again, and make sure each call moves closer to it.

summary: The text is not valid JSON.
causes: The text is empty, or the API/file returned HTML or an error message instead of JSON.
Single quotes used instead of double quotes.
A trailing comma or missing bracket.
fix: Print the raw text before parsing and check it. Validate JSON with a tool such as jsonlint.com.

summary: A file or data was read with the wrong text encoding.
causes: The file is not UTF-8 (often a Windows file or a binary file).
You are opening a binary file, such as an image, in text mode.
fix: Specify the encoding when opening, or open binary files in 'rb' mode.
example:
with open('file.txt', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
    text = f.read()

summary: An assert statement checked a condition that turned out false.
causes: A value is not what the code assumed.
A test expectation does not match the real result.
fix: Print the values used in the assert to see why the condition fails, then fix the data or the expectation.

summary: Python ran out of memory.
causes: Loading a very large file or dataset all at once.
A list or loop that keeps growing without limit.
Creating huge objects, such as a giant range converted to a list.
fix: Process data in smaller pieces instead of loading everything at once, and use generators or chunked reading.
